statement: The Muslims of Madinah went out to the Harrah each morning until the midday heat; one day after they had returned a Jew on a fort saw the Prophet and his companions in white emerging from the mirage and shouted to the Arabs that their great one had come; they took their arms and met him at the Harrah.
notes: Direct speech. Machine-checked against the full text (report of Urwah within Bukhari 3906).

statement: He turned right and alighted among Banu Amr ibn Awf on a Monday in Rabi' al-Awwal; Abu Bakr stood receiving people while he sat silent; those who had not seen him greeted Abu Bakr until Abu Bakr shaded him from the sun and they recognised him.
notes: Machine-checked. That this was at Quba is the standard identification.

statement: He stayed some days in Quba and founded the mosque founded on piety (Qur'an 9:108).
alternatives: Bukhari 3906 says some ten nights; Bukhari 3932 (Anas) says fourteen nights; the Seerah works often say four days.
notes: The script says 'some days' because the reports differ.

statement: He sent for Banu an-Najjar, who came wearing swords; he rode with Abu Bakr behind him and the Ansar around him.
notes: Machine-checked. That Banu an-Najjar were his maternal kin (through Abd al-Muttalib's mother) is from the Seerah.

statement: Anas: news spread through Madinah and people came out looking and saying 'The Prophet of Allah has come'.
notes: Machine-checked. 'Onto the roofs' is from another narration (Muslim, hadith of al-Bara/Abu Bakr); reviewer to confirm or trim.

statement: Al-Bara: I never saw the people of Madinah as joyful as at his arrival.
The report that 'Tala'a al-badru alayna' was sung at his arrival is not established.
notes: Editorial statement. The report is mu'dal (broken chain) per Ibn Hajar and al-Albani, from memory; some place it at the return from Tabuk.

statement: His camel knelt at a date-drying yard belonging to the orphans Sahl and Suhayl under As'ad ibn Zurarah's care; he said 'this, if Allah wills, is the place'; they offered it as a gift; he declined and bought it.
notes: Direct speech. Machine-checked. The dataset translation ends 'then built a mosque there'; that he refused the gift and bought it is in the Arabic of this narration, from memory. Reviewer to confirm.

statement: Abu Ayyub's house was nearest; he said 'this is my house and this is my door'; the Prophet stayed with him.

Abdullah ibn Salam: on seeing his face he knew it was not the face of a liar; the first thing he heard him say was to spread peace, feed others, and pray at night while people sleep, to enter Paradise in peace.
notes: Direct speech. Machine-checked; graded sahih (al-Albani, Ahmad Shakir). Other routes add 'and join the ties of kinship'.

statement: The Companions dated the calendar not from his being sent nor his death but from his arrival in Madinah.
